title: Phase 4: race and fuzz coverage
objective: Prove engine and control state are race-free and that malformed untrusted input produces controlled errors rather than panics or corrupted state.
nonGoals: no sleeps-as-sync anywhere in the tests
nextAction: none; race and fuzz coverage landed. Residuals are recorded in the artifact and in FJ-050.
notes: Picked up 2026-10-03 by PM. Selection reasoning recorded: FJ-040 was chosen over the three gate-tooling tickets (FJ-044 G-L complexity/CRAP, FJ-045 G-H mutation, FJ-046 G-Q system harness) because it is the only remaining candidate that adds genuinely NEW coverage rather than verification plumbing, it is bounded to four new test files with no gate, script or guard wiring and therefore needs no allowedFiles amendment, and it discharges phase-4 acceptance criteria that are core product trust claims (C-QUAL-002 race-freedom, C-QUAL-004 fuzz robustness, C-HOST-009 engine and control state race-free). A system_one second opinion agreed (FJ-040 0.51 vs FJ-046 0.33 vs FJ-062 0.12) but at low confidence 0.43, so the tie was broken on product value: FJ-046's real content is largely wiring a gate row over a harness that already exists in test/integration, so its marginal product value is lower. FJ-046 is the intended next pick for that reason.

Scope facts confirmed before staging: all four allowedFiles targets (internal/engine/race_test.go, internal/control/fuzz_test.go, internal/compat/jev/v1/fuzz_test.go, internal/config/fuzz_test.go) do not exist yet, so this item is net-new test files only. The only pre-existing fuzz target in the repository is FuzzValidateFixtureAnswers in internal/compat/jev/v1/fixture_test.go, added by FJ-059; a second target in a new file in the same package is fine and does not conflict.

Trace ids verified present in docs/development/acceptance-catalog.md: C-HOST-009 (line 97, engine and control state race-free under go test -race, clause 17.4 and 32), C-QUAL-002 (line 168, go test -race ./... passes on supported runners, clause 23), C-QUAL-004 (line 170, fuzz targets show malformed untrusted input yields a controlled error and never a panic or corrupted state, clause 22.2).

KNOWN COST TO FLAG: cmd/guard fuzz runs every discovered fuzz target for guards.json fuzztime (30s). The repository currently has one target, so this item takes the guard fuzz row from roughly 30s to roughly 120s. That is accepted as the price of real fuzz coverage, but it is a deliberate, recorded consequence rather than an accident.

HANDLING RULE FOR GENUINE DEFECTS: allowedFiles covers only the four new test files. If race or fuzz testing exposes a real defect in product code, the defect must NOT be fixed here and product sources must not be edited. Record it in this item's notes as a suspected defect with a minimal reproduction, leave the failing test out or mark it as a skipped documented case, and the PM will open a dedicated follow-up ticket. Open defects already known and therefore likely to surface: the unbounded configuration-file read recorded after FJ-030 (a /dev/zero style input can hang validate), and the post-reset invalid_stub_response recording race in internal/engine/engine.go recorded after FJ-021. Neither may be fixed inside this item.

PARKED 2026-10-03: the coder stage completed and produced candidate 525ee08845fbb909 with the four allowed test files (1148 lines total); the cleaner stage completed and made no change. The hardener stage did not complete because the workflow hit the one-hour harness cap, so no hardener.md exists yet. Nothing was lost - the worktree still holds all four test files, the specifier/coder/cleaner artifacts and the correct chain (specifier in=out=8c80ab29, coder in=8c80ab29 out=525ee08845fb, cleaner in=out=525ee08845fb).

The cleaner produced strong evidence: no sleeps-as-sync, no unseeded randomness, no wall-clock or map-order dependence in any of the four files; per-assertion mutation evidence in a throwaway copy outside the repository; and an explicit disclosure of which assertions are envelope-only and cannot fail (the mixed-test journal-full check is vacuous because capacity 128 versus 72 possible admissions never fills, so the dedicated capacity-64 test is the live journal-full proof). It also flagged two comment over-claims, the sharper one being that internal/config/fuzz_test.go's input cap bounds the input but not the parse cost: a 62,837-byte YAML document using anchors and aliases made one config.Load allocate 51.7 MB in 97 ms, roughly 830x the input, and yaml.v3 permits alias expansion up to about 400k decode operations.

PM HYPOTHESIS recorded for the resumed hardener to test rather than assume: the cleaner observed the config fuzz target freezing or exiting 1 with 'fuzzing process hung or terminated unexpectedly while minimizing: EOF' in about 5 of 8 runs, never in the control or compat targets, and could not attribute it to a slow Load. Minimization only begins after a failure is found, and this target reliably finds F1 and F2 on a cold cache, so the most likely explanation is that the instability is a symptom of the real defects existing (failure then minimization) rather than an independent target bug. The resumed hardener must re-measure config-target stability and guard-fuzz reliability after FJ-064 lands and report the outcome honestly, including if the hypothesis is wrong.
Cleaner already checked one environment artefact: the earlier build-cache corruption recorded on FJ-059 was from low-ulimit fuzz probes and does not affect this item.

RESUMED 2026-10-03 after FJ-064 landed on main (merge commit 340377d). Both defects FJ-040's config fuzz target had found are fixed: config.Load now rejects non-exactly-spelled keys at struct-decoded levels (so the case-variant duplicate-key fail-open is closed and the infinite loop the first fix attempt introduced is gone entirely, because no folding remains), and its diagnostics are deterministic. The FJ-040 worktree now sits on the merged candidate, so the committed coder outputFingerprint 525ee08845fb is no longer the workspace digest: the chain remains specifier in=out=8c80ab29, coder in=8c80ab29 out=525ee08845fb, cleaner in=out=525ee08845fb, and the hardener takes 525ee08845fb as its input and records the new post-merge digest as its output. The four allowed test files are unchanged by this merge.

PARKED AGAIN 2026-10-03 after the QA stage. All five stage artifacts now exist (specifier in=out=8c80ab29, coder in=8c80ab29 out=525ee08845fb, cleaner in=out=525ee08845fb, hardener in=525ee08845fb out=759f71f3, qa in=out=759f71f3). QA verified a great deal successfully - engine mutex removal produced 6 DATA RACE blocks, removed journal-capacity made the conservation assertion fail, and 47 hostile inputs across the three targets behaved; guard fuzz was stable across the PM's 3 runs plus QA's run (findings [], targets 4, about 126s). But QA also found the control-target failure above, which makes the guard fuzz row landmine-like: it passes today only because the 30s window happens not to construct the input, so a green guard row is corpus-dependent. That is precisely the FJ-060 class of problem, on top of a genuine product defect, so FJ-040 must not land until FJ-065 fixes the product. Also recorded by QA and not to be lost: the config target's guard (configFuzzMaxMappingKeys=256) is a TEST-side bound on a TEST-visible symptom, and the hardener itself measured the product-side cost (a 38 KiB input costing 3.14 s and 8.57 GB); once FJ-065 bounds the diagnostic in the product, that test-side guard should be reconsidered rather than left as the only protection. QA additionally noted the control stubMutations lock is not falsifiable through the test, and that section 22.2 matcher-input fuzzing remains uncovered.

RESUMED AGAIN 2026-10-03 after FJ-065 landed at main 433fc97. The control fuzz target's blocker is cleared in principle: FJ-065 stopped the product from echoing yaml.v3's whole duplicate-key diagnostic list, so the control route that previously answered a 640-byte request with 111,424 bytes now answers a constant 107 bytes, and validate on a 30 KB JSON file now writes 102 bytes instead of 271 MB. The hardener must now VERIFY that FJ-040's control fuzz target actually passes on the previously-failing shape rather than assuming it, and must reconsider the test-side bound it previously added to internal/config/fuzz_test.go: configFuzzMaxMappingKeys = 256 was a guard against a symptom in the fuzzer (a 38 KiB input costing 3.14 s and 8.57 GB), and now that the product bounds the reported diagnostic, that guard should be re-justified, reshaped or removed with evidence. Note the residual FJ-065 recorded and the PM accepted: yaml.v3's own duplicate-key comparison is still quadratic for YAML input, so a fuzz target feeding arbitrary bytes can still reach unbounded TIME via the YAML path even though the message is bounded, which is the main reason a bound of some kind may still be justified - the hardener must reason from measurement, not from the previous rationale. The chain so far: specifier in=out=8c80ab29, coder in=8c80ab29 out=525ee08845fb, cleaner in=out=525ee08845fb, hardener in=525ee08845fb out=759f71f3, qa in=out=759f71f3; the hardener now takes 759f71f3 as its input and records the new post-merge digest as its output.

PM CLOSE-OUT 2026-10-03. FJ-040 took four hardener passes and three QA passes, and its own targets found three real defects, two of them in product code, which is exactly what a coverage ticket is for. (1) The config fuzz target found the fail-open case-variant duplicate-key acceptance and the non-deterministic diagnostic; both were fixed under FJ-064 because internal/config was outside FJ-040 allowedFiles. The first fix attempt for that introduced a CRITICAL infinite loop in config.Load on uncased code points (CJK, emoji), which the cleaner caught and the final fix eliminated by abandoning folding for exact-key-spelling rejection. (2) The control fuzz target found response amplification: a tiny createStub request was answered by echoing yaml.v3's entire duplicate-key diagnostic list, 640 bytes in to 111,424 bytes out and 16 KB in to 72.8 MB out. Fixed under FJ-065, which also bounded the diagnostic, took the control route to a constant 107 bytes and made the JSON path flat, while recording (not fixing) the quadratic that remains inside yaml.v3 for YAML input. (3) The second QA pass found that the control regression seed a hardener had added was itself malformed and inert (an extra quote made it 9,608 bytes of invalid JSON rejected before config.Load, so it never exercised the regression it documented); a later hardener pass repaired it to the intended 9,607-byte valid duplicate-key shape, and the final QA confirmed the contrast live: the repaired body yields the 106-byte duplicate-key diagnostic while the malformed one yields the generic 77-byte message. (4) PROCESS INCIDENT: the third QA pass overwrote the second QA pass's completed artifact with a 24-line skeleton when it timed out. The PM reconstructed the full artifact from the run transcript (replaying its initial write plus all seven edits) and preserved it as .agent/work/FJ-040/qa-pass-2.md so the evidence survives; the PM then re-ran the expensive gates itself on the warm cache and had the final QA cite them as PM-run rather than pretend to independent measurement. Root cause of the six harness timeouts on this item is believed to be a COLD Go build cache in each subagent sandbox, which makes any full-suite command take tens of minutes; the mitigation that finally worked was a strictly bounded command list plus writing the artifact before verifying.
